feedback.finish: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria in the body to stop disease.

instruction.text: It is 1928, and a scientist is studying bacteria in 3 different dishes. Find the odd one out.

feedback.end: This dish has no bacteria in it, but a type of mould called penicillin instead.

instruction.text: Why do you think there is no bacteria in the dish?

feedback.finish: The scientist who discovered this, Alexander Fleming, found that penicillin had killed the bacteria. Later, other scientists from Oxford University used this finding to develop the first antibiotic.

instruction.text: Who would have been able to afford good healthcare?

feedback.correct: Although medicine had come a long way, many people still could not afford healthcare, so diseases spread anyway.

instruction.text: The year is 1945. Fill in the gaps in this conversation.

atoms.b: Congratulations on becoming the new Prime ((++Minister Meridian)) Mr Attlee!
Thank you! We have a lot of damage to fix after ((++World_War_Two winter))
One big problem is that lots of people cannot ((++afford attack)) healthcare. We want to give everyone free healthcare with a ((++National Native)) Health Service.
An excellent idea! Everyone deserves to have access to ((++medicine Mexico)). We will pay for it with the money that the government gets from ((++taxes toilets)).
Perfect! Everyone will ((++pay peer)) into it and everyone will benefit from it!

feedback.finish: The NHS started treating patients in 1948 and has continued providing free healthcare up to today!

instruction.text: Modern medicine is very advanced. Match the feature of modern medicine to its name.

feedback.correct: Protective equipment like masks and gloves are important to stop the spread of germs.
Advanced scanning machines can find problems hidden in our bodies.
Modern surgery uses tools like tiny cameras to make operations safe and reliable.
